body: Investigation scope: reconcile three Gemini reconnaissance notes with the current declarative PyTeXML direction, using mechanisms and API contracts as the unit, dependency order as the reading frame, and current code as the external model. The review evolves from a preprocessing-only four-facet schema (D003 H31) through shared argument prototypes (H39) to complete package substitution backed by offline CTAN evidence (H44); the last formulation matches the user's current intent. The six categories in D001 are useful survey facets, not disjoint package kinds. Shared syntax, scoped effects, factories, hooks, and dependency semantics are necessary; neither signature-only YAML nor named operation strings alone establish completeness. Unsupported percentages, mechanical migration guarantees, and guaranteed local recovery are unproven in these notes.

Proposed synthesis: standardize the behavioral vocabulary and runtime protocol alongside YAML schemas. A shared catalog compiles package declarations; lookup/start/step interleaves scanners and timed scoped effects using the shared cursor; the same vocabulary supports runtime author declarations without temporary YAML. Preparation selects effects necessary for faithful reading and source closure, with their prerequisites; later interpretation adds semantic construction. This is broader than prototypes plus XML templates. Keep one authored package binding; distinguish package evidence, operation implementation, policy, and output representation. A missing closing delimiter or unknown reading effect can leave an unresolved suffix, so span geometry alone cannot certify recovery. Source-span-engine.md already states staged dispatch and certified recovery; use it as the anchor rather than multiplying overlapping specs. Existing ReaderContext only applies immediate effects and the resolver still hardcodes some profile selection, so an implemented generic runtime has not yet been established.
